dismissedFlows.title: Start bookclub and manage a book on the shelf
dismissedFlows.note: A nine-milestone tour of the whole product in one test. Every milestone it walks is already asserted by a focused flow (check-service-health, require-member-token-to-add-a-book, add-a-duplicate-isbn, handle-missing-book-details); bundling them adds no coverage and no single scenario expresses them faithfully.

dismissedFlows.title: Add, list, get, and finish a book
dismissedFlows.note: A five-milestone tour across four sections, duplicating flows that already pass one behaviour at a time. It also walks the experimental cover endpoint, which is deliberately outside the published contract in docs/openapi.yaml.

dismissedFlows.title: Run the service
dismissedFlows.note: A startup tour bundling configuration defaults, boot migrations, the startup log line and the health probe into one test. The health behaviour is asserted by check-service-health and the configuration defaults by print-configuration-with-a-redacted-database-password.

dismissedFlows.title: Keep a member token working after restart
dismissedFlows.note: Asserting this needs the service restarted midway through a single scenario, which the api driver cannot express — a scenario boots one server. The statelessness it rests on is a property of the token, not an endpoint response.

dismissedFlows.title: Finish and re-finish a book
dismissedFlows.note: Re-stamping can only be shown by comparing two finishedAt timestamps across steps, which the expectation vocabulary cannot state. The finish behaviour itself is asserted by require-member-token-to-finish-a-book and handle-finishing-an-unknown-book.

dismissedFlows.title: Add a book and prevent another copy of the same ISBN
dismissedFlows.note: Bundles ISBN normalisation with the one-copy-per-ISBN refusal; the fidelity reviewer rejects every authored form of the pair. Both halves already pass on their own — reject-an-invalid-isbn covers normalisation and add-a-duplicate-isbn covers the 409.
